_comment: HOW MANY THINGS EACH GATE MUST HAVE LOOKED AT BEFORE IT IS ALLOWED TO SAY
'pass'. A ratchet in the same sense as scripts/coverage-floor.json: the gate
fails when the number drops BELOW these, never for being above them, and it
does not raise itself.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The 2026-09-08 sweep of the released v0.2.3 found the
same bug twice, in two unrelated gates, and it is the most expensive bug
shape this repository has produced:
A SELECTOR THAT MATCHES NOTHING RETURNS SUCCESS.
- `pnpm --filter gnomon-cli` matched nothing once the package was renamed
gnomon-harness for npm, and pnpm exits 0 when only SOME filters match.
Three CI jobs kept exiting 0 while running three packages of four. The
106 CLI tests stopped running on windows-latest and macos-latest — the
exact two platforms whose path and shell handling those tests exist to
cover — and nothing anywhere went red for two releases.
- .gnomon/ci.sh's portability gate used the git pathspec
`benchmarks/**/*.py`. A `**/` pathspec requires at least one
intermediate directory, so the five files that ARE the apparatus, all
sitting directly in benchmarks/, were never scanned. The gate read green
over 98 files while 103 were in scope.
Neither was a wrong answer. Both were a gate reporting success having
checked less than it claimed, which is worse than a failure: a red gate gets
fixed and a vacuous green one gets trusted.
WHAT A FLOOR IS AND IS NOT. It is a smoke alarm for scope collapse, not an
assertion about the codebase. Set each one well below today's number, far
enough that ordinary work never trips it and a selector breaking always
does. A floor set AT the current count would fail on the first deleted test
and be switched off within a month — the same reasoning coverage-floor.json
already records.
PREFER A DERIVED IDENTITY WHERE ONE EXISTS. ts-packages has no floor here
because it does not need one: the gate compares the packages that REPORTED
against the workspace packages that DECLARE a test script, so adding a
package raises the requirement automatically and no number here can go
stale. A floor is the fallback for sets with nothing to derive from.
Measured 2026-09-09 at: rust-tests 60, ts-tests 1070, benchmark-adapters 3,
apparatus-files 102.

rust-tests.why: cargo test --all across four crates. Dropping under 40 means a crate stopped being compiled or `--all` stopped meaning all, not that tests were deleted.

ts-tests.why: The whole TypeScript suite. gnomon-core alone is over 900; anything under 800 means a package did not run, which is the shape of the --filter bug rather than of deleted tests.

benchmark-adapters.why: Committed *gnomon_agent.py adapters. At zero the clock-parity gate has nothing to check and used to say so and pass — a rename of the adapter file would have silently retired the gate that exists because this bug class recurred twice.

apparatus-files.why: Tracked .sh/.mjs/.js/.py under benchmarks/ and scripts/ that the portability gate scans. The broken pathspec saw 98 of 103; a floor here would not have caught that five-file gap, but it does catch the pathspec breaking outright, which is the failure mode that retires the gate completely.
